exact_claim_text: Within the declared synthetic scenarios, token-bucket control reduces false rejection under moderate burstiness relative to fixed-window control, while its queue-tail advantage does not persist under sustained near-saturation load.
method_or_source: Token-bucket versus fixed-window, checked against hand-calculated limiting cases and a no-control reference.
uncertainty: Monte Carlo variation, sensitivity to arrival and service assumptions, implementation error and scenario-selection bias.
boundary: Synthetic discrete-event simulation; one service pool; no production traffic, user data or deployment claim.
counter_evidence: Illustrative values only: at offered load 0.70 and moderate burstiness, the worked dataset records false rejection of 8.4% for fixed-window and 5.7% for token-bucket; at offered load 0.95, the token-bucket scenario shows a materially longer queue tail.
stronger_wording_rejected: Token-bucket control is superior for production APIs.
